item.title: Free energy fluctuations of symmetric perceptron models up to and including criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.31736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the free energy fluctuations of spherical and Ising perceptron models with general even activations. These include the symmetric binary perceptron, the $U$-perceptron, and the bipartite Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main result is a Gaussian CLT for the free energy that holds both in the ``high-temperature'' interior of a second moment RS regime and on its ``critical'' boundary. At criticality, the CLT has scale $(\frac{\log N}{6})^{1/2}$, which matches the free energy fluctuations of the critical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model and suggests this scaling is universal. The proof shows that the perceptron model's free energy fluctuations are explained, up to an additive $o(1)$ error with high probability, by those of a corresponding spherical Hopfield model, and that this relation persists even at criticality. This proof strategy builds on a critical reweighted moment method developed by the first and third authors \cite{du2026fluctuations} to identify the critical fluctuations of the SK free energy, which links these fluctuations to the spectral edge spacing of the disorder.
item.dc:creator: Hang Du, Shuyang Gong, Brice Huang, Zhangsong Li

item.title: Random Cellular Automata and deBruijn Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Update rules of a one dimensional Cellular Automaton can be expressed using an edge-labeled deBruijn graph. We explore various questions about the image of a cellular automaton given by a randomly selected update rule by considering a random deBruijn graph.
item.dc:creator: Janko Gravner, Travis Kulhanek

item.title: Probabilistic representation and Monte Carlo method for nonlinear Dirac equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dirac equations describe the relativistic evolution of quantum particles. Using the point-process stochastic calculus of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) on general state spaces, which naturally allows additional Feynman-Kac potentials, we develop a probabilistic representation for the nonlinear Dirac equations in $1+1$ spacetime dimension with cubic nonlinearity and $L_\infty$-type problem data using a multi-type branching telegraph process together with both continuous and jump-type multiplicative functionals. Our main theorem leads to a classification result which, when applied to the specific Soler model, gives a sharp finite-time admissibility of the probabilistic representation. By extending the one-step representation to a multi-step, time-marching representation using an analytically-derived a priori $L_\infty$ estimate, we observe a ``local probabilistic representation, but global PDE well-posedness" phenomenon. We proceed to propose a time-marching Monte Carlo algorithm as a global numerical solver for the Soler system with a rigorous convergence proof and establish an additional stability result on the PDE side. Finally, while the underlying process parameters do not affect the validity of the probabilistic representation, we observe their potential for variance reduction in the Monte Carlo methods.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Fouque, Tomoyuki Ichiba, Ka Lok Lam

item.title: Reflected BSDEs under random horizons: Sharp support criteria, irregular reflection, and Cox reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.31988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study reduction and reconstruction of reflected backward stochastic differential equations (RBSDEs) across random horizons. We establish optional and predictable contact-measure transfer criteria by dual projection, prove a Cox survival identity for arbitrary integrable reflection measures (including atoms), and give a Brownian Cox reconstruction theorem with continuous obstacles and a converse within a specified reduction class. We also isolate componentwise minimality criteria for irregular obstacles and predictable reflection. The unresolved semimartingale and obstacle transport problems for general non-Cox invariance times are formulated as open questions rather than asserted as theorems. The paper distinguishes established results from conditional constructions.
item.dc:creator: Youssef Ouknine, Badr Elmansouri

item.title: Graph distance and percolation dimension of three-dimensional Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2610.32137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the minimum Hausdorff dimension of a continuous curve joining $W_0$ to $W_1$ within the range $W([0,1])$ of a three-dimensional Brownian motion is almost surely a deterministic constant $\gamma_3\in(1,5/3]$. Moreover, we construct continuum many simple curves with pairwise distinct images that attain this minimum. Each curve has box dimension $\gamma_3$ and admits a parametrization that is $\beta$-H\"older for every $0<\beta<1/\gamma_3$. To identify $\gamma_3$, we partition Brownian time into $n$ equal intervals and form a graph by joining pairs with intersecting ranges. We show that its endpoint graph distance and diameter have a common deterministic almost sure growth exponent $\theta$ and that $\gamma_3=2\theta$. We also establish $n^{p\theta+o(1)}$ growth for their $p$-th moments, for every $p>0$.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Shiraishi

item.title: Rough path lifts of multifractional Brownian motions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that multifractional Brownian motions (mBms) can be lifted to geometric rough paths. One of the main ingredients in the proof is a decomposition of mBms via the Lemari\'e-Meyer orthogonal wavelet basis, which is introduced in the context of multiresolution analysis. As a consequence, we are able to construct solutions to rough differential equations driven by mBms.
item.dc:creator: Nobuaki Naganuma

item.title: Wasserstein bounds for invariant measures in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation with stable noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.32217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study invariant position distributions in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation for Langevin equations driven by rotationally symmetric \(\alpha\)-stable noise, with \(\alpha\in(1,2)\). Under global Lipschitz continuity and dissipativity of the drift, we establish a Wasserstein-1 bound of order \(m^{1/\alpha}\) between the invariant position distribution of the underdamped system and the invariant distribution of its overdamped limit, where $m>0$ is the mass parameter. The proof combines a corrected-position test function with a regularized Stein equation. Cancellation of the transport and friction terms reduces the comparison to a first-moment estimate for the stationary velocity.
item.dc:creator: Xinghu Jin, Wenxuan Tao

item.title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
item.description: arXiv:2610.32649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.
item.dc:creator: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: How much do increasing events occur disjointly?
item.description: arXiv:2610.32658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish two general quantitative lower bounds on the gap in the classical BK inequality for increasing events. The first is an analogue of Talagrand's quantitative FKG inequality (1996) and depends on the influences. The second is specific to the BK inequality and involves both the influences and the probabilities of symmetric disjoint pivots.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Tesio

item.title: The Martingale Property in Volterra Volatility Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.32684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study martingality and strict local martingality in a broad class of stochastic and path-dependent Volterra volatility models and explain the underlying mechanisms. Our martingality criteria allow rough kernels and rely on non-accessibility of an explosive direction or one-sided growth bounds on the Girsanov drift. For smooth kernels, we derive sufficient conditions for strict local martingality from an explosion criterion allowing multiplicative noise, coupled factors and general initial input curves. Our results recover classical criteria and yield new results for Volterra and path-dependent models.
item.dc:creator: Julien Guyon, Thibault Jeannin, Benjamin Jourdain

item.title: Avalanches of the Abelian sandpile on the hierarchical lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.32687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Abelian sandpile model on a sequence of finite fractal graphs: the hierarchical, or Migdal--Kadanoff, lattices. Our first main result consists of matching power-law tail bounds for the avalanche and the uniform wave started at certain "pivotal" vertices. We also establish a limiting result for the pivotal reach of the avalanche and, finally, a scaling limit for the size of a uniform wave started at a vertex of high degree.
item.dc:creator: Luca Cattani, Leandro Chiarini, Alessandra Cipriani

item.title: Non-equilibrium density fluctuations for the stirring process with weak boundary dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.32701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the one-dimensional stirring process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We investigate the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the system, starting from a product measure associated with a smooth initial profile. The limit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is given in terms of the Laplacian and gradient operators acting on test functions satisfying time-dependent Robin boundary conditions that are obtained by linearizing the boundary conditions in the hydrodynamic equation. A central ingredient in our analysis is the derivation of sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree for the centered occupation variables; these bounds were proved in the companion article \cite{birmpa2025nonequilibriumfluctuationsstirringprocess}.
item.dc:creator: Panagiota Birmpa, Patr\'icia Gon\c{c}alves, Dimitrios Tsagkarogiannis

item.title: The boosted loop-erased random walk
item.description: arXiv:2610.32821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a near-critical version of loop-erased random walk (LERW) by boosting the weight of the underlying random walk according to its length before loop-erasure. We construct the scaling limit in natural parametrization in the two-dimensional unit disk and the three-dimensional unit ball. The boosted scaling limit undergoes a phase transition in mutual absolute continuity with the classical LERW scaling limit; in the disk the transition occurs at boost rate $m^2=\pi^2/4$. As the boost increases, the curve becomes macroscopically space-filling, in the sense that unvisited cubes have side length $O(m^{-1})$, while its Hausdorff dimension at each finite boost is unchanged. These results are motivated by Makarov--Smirnov's questions on near-critical lattice models. In the planar chordal setting, we also construct a continuum loop tilt below the spectral threshold of the domain and calculate its Loewner driving function.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai, Xinyi Li, Daisuke Shiraishi, Aoteng Xia

item.title: Near-critical Ising interfaces in the thermal direction: Absolute continuity with respect to SLE$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.32860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scaling limits of interfaces in the critical two-dimensional Ising model are described by the Schramm--Loewner evolution $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. While, in the scaling limit, the law of the whole near-critical FK-Ising configuration is known to be singular with respect to the critical law in the thermal direction, and the same is expected for the spin configuration, we prove in this paper that the law of a single interface is not. More precisely, we consider the Ising model with mesh $\delta$ in the Dobrushin square at $\beta=\beta_c-m\delta$, where $m\ne0$ is fixed, and we prove that the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the law of the interface with respect to its critical law has moments of every positive and negative order, bounded uniformly in $\delta$, so that the law of every subsequential scaling limit of the interface is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to that of $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. Our analysis explains the mechanism behind this result: the logarithmically growing specific heat (that is, the variance of the Hamiltonian, normalized by the number of edges) cancels between the full domain and the domain slit along the interface.
item.dc:creator: Yu Feng

item.title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $\eta\in(0,1)$. We study the large deviation rate of the lower tail event $T_n\le\eta\mathbb{E}[T_n]$, and the typical structure of $G(n,p)$ conditioned on this event. By earlier work [16,19,21,49], both the rate and the structure are governed by a variational problem over graphons. In this work we solve this variational problem for every $\eta\in(0,1)$. We show that every minimizer is either a constant graphon or a step graphon with two blocks of equal size. Correspondingly, the conditioned graph is close to an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph or to a symmetric stochastic block model with two blocks. These two regimes are separated by a first order phase transition at the threshold $\eta_*=0.009217\ldots$. This resolves a conjecture of Zhao [78] and an open problem of Janson and Warnke [39] on triangles. It thereby gives a complete description of the lower tail of triangle counts in this range of $p$.
item.dc:creator: Dong Huang, Shuangping Li

item.title: Probabilistic ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model
item.description: arXiv:2610.32927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a probabilistic approach to the ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model. The model is formally described by the density $\exp(\alpha\int \mathopen{:} \cos(\beta X) \mathclose{:} )$, where $X$ is a log-correlated Gaussian field. Our construction applies on bounded convex domains for every particle activity $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and throughout the subcritical range $\beta^2\in[0,4)$, below the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless threshold. We apply the martingale method introduced by Lacoin, Rhodes and Vargas to two dimensions by using refined estimates based on charge conjugation symmetries. Our result extends existing constructions by treating the full subcritical regime for a broad class of covariances.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Bonnefont, Hermanni Rajam\"aki, Vincent Vargas

item.title: A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.32942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a supercritical two-type continuous-time linear birth-death process with mutation and selection, in which wild-type individuals give rise to mutant offspring with a larger net-growth rate. We previously had obtained first-order law of large number results for the driver site frequency spectrum. We return to obtain a second-order central limit theorem, in which we show stable convergence of a scaling of the deviation of the SFS from its first-order limit. We provide a central limit theorem at both large detection times and sizes. Then, we apply these results to obtain confidence intervals for a class of consistent estimators for the fitness advance.
item.dc:creator: Armaan Ahmed, Jasmine Foo, Kevin Leder

item.title: Early learning in large residual networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.31783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the early training dynamics of nonlinear residual networks with blocks of zero hidden layers as a model of more general residual networks. We analyze networks in a sequential limit where first width and depth diverge, then the number of training data points diverges, and finally the input dimension diverges. This is a more refined setup compared to the typical mean-field theory analysis in which depth and width diverge but the number of training datapoints and input dimension are fixed. Our main technical result is a diagrammatic computation of both the network output and the hidden representations after the few steps of gradient descent in terms of the statistics of inner products of inputs from the training set. One of our principle conceptual findings is a negative result: in the limit of large input dimension the network output can learn only a linear function of its inputs early in training since higher learned monomials are more and more suppressed in the input dimension and vanish in the large dimension limit. This suggests that mean-field limits of ResNets are surprisingly rigid in the regime of high input dimension and may not be sufficient toy models for understanding feature learning. Finally, we investigate how to ensure hyperparameter transfer for the learning rate as a function of dataset size and input dimension. We test our predictions numerically and find excellent agreement with our theory.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Narovlansky, Boris Hanin

item.title: Mimicking Volatilities under Marginal Constraints via $q_x$-Bass Martingales: A Parallel Computing Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.31825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the calibration of continuous-time martingale models to observed derivative prices via a dynamic martingale optimal transport problem that penalizes deviations from the volatility of a prescribed reference model. Using $q_x$-Bass martingales, we approximate this problem through a sequence of discrete-time problems and prove that the continuous-time interpolations of their optimizers are asymptotically optimal. Building on the theory of $q_x$-Bass martingales, we develop numerical methods for the discrete-time problems that do not require full marginal distributions at calibration maturities.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Marini

item.title: On the Propeller Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.32158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We simplify and improve OpenAI's proof of the propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor from 2008: the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian moments of any partition of Euclidean space is at most $9/(8\pi)$. We show equality only occurs for three 120 degree sectors in the plane (up to symmetries, measure zero changes, and taking orthogonal cross products with Euclidean space). We also remove computer assistance from the three-dimensional case of the conjecture, which previously used an epsilon net traversal.
item.dc:creator: Steven Heilman

item.title: A stochastic mirror descent algorithm for mean-field control problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a stochastic mirror descent method for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov control with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularisation. The dependence on the state law leads to a coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability problem and to a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation, which have no counterpart in classical stochastic control. We establish a first-order representation of the cost and prove its relative smoothness in two regimes: nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives, and affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing cost derivatives, the latter covering linear-quadratic (LQ) and more general nonquadratic models. Our regularity conditions in the control measure are formulated through directional finite increments and do not require second-order flat derivatives. We further introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories, allowing compensation between the dynamics, running cost, and terminal cost beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity. This yields energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularisation dominates relative nonconvexity. Explicit LQ criteria and numerical experiments illustrate the scope of the results.
item.dc:creator: Noufel Frikha (CES), Aymen Haouas (X)

item.title: Optimality of finite field dimension expanders
item.description: arXiv:2610.32394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that random tuples of matrices over a finite field are uniform dimension expanders for every expansion coefficient below the optimal one, using elementary counting arguments. The same holds for the optimal coefficient along a set of dimensions of density 1. By contrast, along Fibonacci dimensions random pairs of matrices fail to be optimal dimension expanders with probability bounded away from zero.
item.dc:creator: Urban Jezernik, Markus Reineke

item.title: On the closure under barycenters of location-scatter families with a normalized generator
item.description: arXiv:2610.32446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide an example of a normalized absolutely continuous probability whose location-scatter family (LSF) does not contain all the 2-Wassertein geodesics passing through its elements. In particular, we find a counterexample for Corollary 4.5 in [2]. Finally, we prove that LSFs with a (possibly singular) radially symmetric generator are closed under 2-Wasserstein barycenters.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Aldrigo

item.title: Stochastic predator-prey compartment model with cyclic and non-cyclic transition pathways and mortality
item.description: arXiv:2610.32535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study variants of a stochastic SEIRS-SEID compartmental model incorporating presymptomatic infectiousness and disease-related mortality, with independent compartmental sojourn times drawn from arbitrary distributions, in particular Weibull distributions. We consider a large population of agents that occupy the states (compartments) S (susceptible to infection), E (exposed: infected but asymptomatic during the latency period and already infectious, including diseases with presymptomatic infections), I (infected and infectious, with symptoms), R (recovered, immune, and non-infectious), or D (dead). We consider (i) cyclic transmission pathways, where compartmental sojourn times are finite and immunity is temporary, and (ii) non-cyclic pathways, where immunity is permanent. In the absence of mortality, cyclic transmission pathways support an endemic equilibrium above the spreading threshold which is either globally stable or oscillatory (Hopf) unstable, whereas for non-cyclic pathways a stationary disease-free state is emerging. From a stochastic perspective, we elucidate the connection between compartmental sojourn-time distributions and the appearance of fractional operators in the evolution equations: fat-tailed compartment waiting-time distributions necessarily lead to fractional derivatives. For cyclic transition pathways we obtain an explicit expression for the expected number of infection cycles that an agent survives. Our model is validated by a combined Monte Carlo -- Runge -- Kutta simulation scheme and random-walk simulations on Barabasi-Albert networks. It has cross-disciplinary applications beyond epidemiology, including wildfire spreading, certain classes of chemical reactions, population dynamics, finance, economics, and biology.
item.dc:creator: Thomas M. Michelitsch, Ayten D. Baher, Michael Bestehorn, Andrzej F. Nowakowski, Alejandro P. Riascos, Bernard A. Collet

item.title: On Trace Averages and Sharp Asymptotics for Powers of Haar-Unitary Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a Haar-distributed matrix $U \in U(N)$, Rains's power-map theorem represents the spectrum of $U^m$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, as a superposition of independent lower-dimensional CUE spectra. We determine how this exact decomposition appears in trace moments and in sharp Gaussian and Poisson limit laws. For averages of mixed trace products, a Charlier--Ewens convolution separates the stable Wick term from its full finite-$N$ correction. A Fredholm factorisation gives sharp total-variation asymptotics for the normalised trace in four regimes, from fixed powers to $m\geq N$. For a fixed trace power $p$, coherent summation of the leading Laguerre correction yields the exact factor $e^{2/p}$. At the mean-spacing scale, we obtain a sharp Poisson limit for the unfolded spectrum of $U^m$ on a fixed interval as $N, m \rightarrow \infty$; its first-order correction, obtained via the second Charlier polynomial, quantifies the residual under-dispersion of local eigenvalue counts.
item.dc:creator: Ayesha Irfan

item.title: The solution of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns
item.description: arXiv:2610.32618v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the free energy of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $\alpha$ and temperature $T$, and we give it as an explicit variational principle. The Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation maps the model onto $N$ Ising spins coupled to $M=\alpha N$ Gaussian hidden units, whose radius, the empirical variance of the hidden layer, is a thermodynamic variable with an entropic cost. At fixed radius the model is an Ising--spherical spin glass with Gaussian couplings, which we solve. The principle (i) reproduces the Amit-Gutfreund-Sompolinsky theory as its replica-symmetric restriction, (ii) identifies $T_g=1+\sqrt\alpha$ as the rigorous boundary of the annealed region, (iii) selects a unique spin-glass solution of the AGS equations, and (iv) gives the radius an equation of state. Moreover, (v) below $T_g$ we prove that replica symmetry is broken throughout: the instability of the AGS solution reduces to the zero-field de Almeida-Thouless condition of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Camilli, Pierluigi Contucci, Emanuele Mingione

item.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
item.description: arXiv:2610.32829v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.
item.dc:creator: Lo\"is Delande (AGM - UMR 8088), Tony Leli\`evre (CERMICS), Boris Nectoux (LMBP), Thomas Normand

item.title: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing
item.description: arXiv:2610.32970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stratification can reduce the estimator variance in Monte Carlo simulations by partitioning the sample space according to a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within the resulting strata, making it well suited to the valuation of path-dependent claims in high-dimensional financial models. Its performance, however, depends critically on the choice of the stratification factor, and effective low-dimensional factors are generally difficult to identify in complex continuous-time models. Neural networks provide a flexible approximation class for this purpose and have proved useful in related variance-reduction problems in quantitative finance. In this paper, we study the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. Since the numerical construction of a stratification factor typically involves approximation, we establish continuity results for the associated conditional expectations and, more generally, conditional distributions, and provide several counterexamples showing the limits of this continuity theory. Combined with density results for neural networks, our findings yield a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. We conclude with numerical experiments involving a constant-maturity-swap range accrual in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a worst-of autocallable in a Wishart stochastic covariance model, where the learned factors outperform all considered benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandar Arandjelovic, Patrick Cheridito

item.title: Construction and sample path properties of diffusion house-moving between two curves
item.description: arXiv:2503.16912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This study aims to construct a stochastic process called ``diffusion house-moving,'' which is a diffusion bridge conditioned to stay between its starting point and its ending point. To construct this process, statements are prepared on the weak convergence of conditioned diffusion processes, and conditioned diffusion bridges. Moreover, the sample path properties of diffusion house-moving are studied as well.
item.dc:creator: Kensuke Ishitani, Soma Nishino

item.title: General diffusions on metric graphs as limits of space-time Markov chains
item.description: arXiv:2507.23724v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the Space-Time Markov Chain Approximation (STMCA) for a general diffusion process on a finite metric graph $\Gamma$. The STMCA is a doubly asymmetric (in both time and space) random walk defined on subdivisions of $\Gamma$, with transition probabilities and conditional transition times that match, in expectation, those of the target diffusion. We derive bounds on the $p$-Wasserstein distances between a non-explosive diffusion and its STMCA in terms of a thinness quantifier of the subdivision. An extension to absorbed diffusions uses a boundary-adapted Green-kernel thinness that remains finite even at certain singular exit boundaries. Under the stated regularity and subdivision hypotheses, this gives convergence at any rate strictly less than $\frac14\wedge\frac1p$ in the appropriate thinness quantifier. For suitably adapted subdivisions satisfying a quadratic thinness bound, we show that the rate is doubled: we achieve any rate strictly less than $\frac12\wedge\frac2p$ in terms of the maximum cell size. Additionally, we provide explicit analytical formulas for transition probabilities and times, enabling practical implementation of the STMCA, as well as easily verifiable sufficient non-explosion conditions for the bounds to hold. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Anagnostakis

item.title: Limit theorems for supercritical branching processes in Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions
item.description: arXiv:2607.04759v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behaviour for distribution of supercritical branching process in a Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions. Phase transitions in the behaviour of the process is discovered, through investigating the strongly, intermediately and weakly supercritical cases.
item.dc:creator: Yinna Ye, Quansheng Liu

item.title: Discrete Approximation to Time-changed Brownian Motions
item.description: arXiv:2609.07789v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a general discrete approximation scheme for time-changed Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approximation scheme works for any smooth measure with full quasi-support on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with suitable initial distributions. Under some mild conditions on the smooth measure, the discrete approximation scheme works for every starting point. Our results in particular give a discrete approximation scheme for Liouville Brownian motions.
item.dc:creator: Zhen-Qing Chen, Yang Yu

item.title: Second-order perturbation bounds for Gibbs samplers under strong spatial mixing
item.description: arXiv:2609.13495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The basic question in perturbation analysis of Markov chains is how small changes in their transition kernels affect their stationary distributions. Classical perturbation bounds typically require the kernel error to be much smaller than $1/\tau$, where $\tau$ is a mixing or relaxation time. Although this scaling is sharp for Markov chains in general, we investigate a general "square-rooting" phenomenon in which one-step errors of order roughly $1/\sqrt{\tau}$ can be sufficient for local updates. We proved a form of this phenomenon in Lin, Liu and Smith (2025) under strong assumptions. Here we substantially weaken these assumptions, and prove this phenomenon occurs using three distinct approaches. First, block factorization applies under structural assumptions on the stationary measures of both chains. Second, approximate block-update arguments extend the result to statistically relevant Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) settings, where structural guarantees are available for the exact posterior and its associated sampler, but not for the perturbed posterior. Third, we use direct calculations for a class of models with hard constraints where neither general result is directly available. We illustrate these results in three MCMC settings and show how they directly inform the tuning of approximate MCMC algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Na Lin, Aaron Smith, Yiqiang Q. Zhao

item.title: Conditional Stable Laws and Rare-Event Limits for Absorbing Markov Chains
item.description: arXiv:2609.22499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish conditional limit theorems, pointwise in the initial state, for absorbing Markov chains on a compact metric space $M$. We assume $L^1(M,\rho)$-continuous transition densities, irreducibility and aperiodicity. For the observable $f_\beta(x)=d_M(x,x_0)^{-\beta}$, with suitable $x_0$ satisfying $\rho(B_r(x_0))\sim C_d(x_0)r^d$, we prove that the point-process of normalised observations converges to a Poisson random measure. This yields totally right-skewed $\alpha$-stable laws for $\alpha=d/\beta\in(0,2)$ and, at the boundary value $\alpha=2$, a Gaussian limit with the non-standard normalisation $\sqrt{n\log n}$. We also establish a conditional central limit theorem for $L^2$ observables, exponential deviation bounds for bounded observables and a conditional Poisson law for visits to shrinking targets. The results and remarks have been formalised in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Bassols Cornudella, Matheus M Castro

item.title: The Fixed-$q$ Edge Limit of the $q$-Krawtchouk Ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2609.24149v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the fixed-$q$ right-edge asymptotics of the ordinary $q$-Krawtchouk ensemble. For $0<q<1$, finite polynomial duality gives a direct proof of convergence of the correlation kernels to an explicit limiting kernel. The local Jacobi limit is a shifted continuous $q^{-1}$-Hermite expression with an indeterminate moment problem, so the limiting Jacobi expression does not determine a unique self-adjoint operator. A single spectral atom, asymptotically saturating the mass bound, selects the realization and yields strong-resolvent convergence. The limiting kernel represents its positive spectral projection and admits spectral-series, Christoffel--Darboux, and partial-theta representations. After a ground-state transformation, the associated dual operator agrees with a two-step spatial Markov operator of Borodin--Corwin. For $q>1$, the limiting Jacobi operator is of Al-Salam--Carlitz~I type and is essentially self-adjoint.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Nikitin

item.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous-Broder Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Aldous-Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but deriving it by summing over the orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered remains difficult. In this paper, we evaluate this sum by establishing an order-mass identity for rooted forests. For real matrices with zero row sums, the identity expresses the sum of order weights associated with each root as a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots, under a nonsingularity condition involving only the sets encountered along the growth orders of the given forest. We prove the identity using linear algebraic tools. With one root, the sum equals one, giving a direct proof of the extended Aldous-Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state. With multiple roots, we derive the forest law produced by the stopped covering walk and show how it differs from the weight-proportional forest law. The identity and the resulting tree and forest laws are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Hugh Zheng

item.title: Stochastic Inverse Problem: stability, regularization and Wasserstein gradient flow
item.description: arXiv:2410.00229v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inverse problems in physical or biological sciences often involve recovering an unknown parameter that is random. The sought-after quantity is a probability distribution of the unknown parameter, that produces data that aligns with measurements. Consequently, these problems are naturally framed as stochastic inverse problems. In this paper, we explore three aspects of this problem: direct inversion, variational formulation with regularization, and optimization via gradient flows, drawing parallels with deterministic inverse problems. A key difference from the deterministic case is the space in which we operate. Here, we work within a probability space rather than Euclidean or Sobolev spaces, making tools from measure transport theory necessary for the study. Our findings reveal that the choice of metric---both in the design of the loss function and in the optimization process---significantly impacts the stability and properties of the optimizer.
item.dc:creator: Qin Li, Maria Oprea, Li Wang, Yunan Yang

item.title: Uniform ergodicity and spectral gap of importance-tempered MCMC with heavy-tailed targets
item.description: arXiv:2506.19186v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the importance-tempered random-walk Metropolis (RWM) algorithm on $\mathbb{R}^d$, which targets the tempered density $\pi_\beta(x) \propto \pi(x)^\beta$ with $\beta \in (0,1)$ and corrects for the resulting bias by importance weighting. The dynamics of this sampler can be described by a continuous-time Markov chain whose embedded chain is the tempered RWM. We prove that when the tails of $\pi$ decay at rate $\|x\|^{-\gamma}$, this continuous-time chain is uniformly ergodic if and only if $d/\gamma < \beta < (\gamma - 2)/\gamma$. Further, the global spectral gap of this chain can be controlled via the spectral gap of the chain restricted to a ball with radius growing polynomially in $d$. Our theory and simulation studies show that, with a suitable choice of $\beta$, importance tempering can substantially reduce sensitivity to initialization and significantly improve efficiency over the standard RWM.
item.dc:creator: Quan Zhou

item.title: Perfect t-Embeddings of Uniformly Weighted Generalized Tower Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.18791v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study sequences of perfect t-embeddings of a uniformly weighted family of graphs we call generalized tower graphs. We show that the embeddings of these graphs satisfy certain technical assumptions, in particular, the rigidity assumption of Berggren-Nicoletti-Russkikh. As a result, we confirm the convergence of the gradients of the height function fluctuations of these graphs to those of the Gaussian free field.
item.dc:creator: David Keating, Hieu Trung Vu

item.title: Superpixel-Based Image Segmentation Using Squared 2-Wasserstein Distances
item.description: arXiv:2601.17071v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an efficient method for image segmentation in the presence of strong intensity inhomogeneities. The approach combines two levels of clustering: pixels are first grouped into superpixels using Power-SLIC, which admits a discrete optimal transport (OT) interpretation, and these superpixels are subsequently merged using squared 2-Wasserstein distances between their empirical distributions. We formulate the merging process as an adjacency-constrained hierarchical optimization problem with a regularized objective that accounts for the heterogeneities of previously formed regions. We establish NP-completeness of the associated global optimization problem, even for two final regions and two-bin histograms. For the proposed greedy algorithm, we prove exact recovery under suitable histogram separation conditions and derive an additive approximation bound for the regularized energy. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive segmentation accuracy on images exhibiting substantial intensity inhomogeneity, while retaining computational efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Jisui Huang, Andreas Alpers, Ke Chen, Na Lei

item.title: On the $q$-integrability of $p$-Wasserstein barycenters
item.description: arXiv:2602.18293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the $L^q$-regularity of the density of barycenters of $N$ probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to the $p$-Wasserstein metric ($1<p<\infty$). According to a previous result by the first author and collaborators, if one marginal is absolutely continuous, so is the $W_p$-barycenter. The next natural question is whether the $L^q$- regularity on the marginals is also preserved for any $q > 1$, as in the classical case ($p=2$) of Agueh--Carlier, or for $W_p$-geodesics ($N=2$). Here we prove that this is the case if one marginal belongs to $L^q$ and the supports of all the marginals satisfy suitable geometric assumptions. However, we show that, as soon as $N>2$, it is possible to find examples of $W_p$-barycenters which are not $q$-integrable, even if one marginal is compactly supported and bounded, thus highlighting the role played by the geometry of the supports. Furthermore, we provide a general estimate of the $L^q$-norm, including a detailed study of the sources of singularities, and a characterization of the $W_p$-barycenters \`a la Agueh--Carlier in terms of the associated Kantorovich potentials. Finally, we explicitly compute the $W_p$-barycenters of measures obtained as push-forward of special affine transformations. In this case, regularity holds without any additional requirement on the supports.
item.dc:creator: Camilla Brizzi, Lorenzo Portinale

item.title: Generalized fluctuation bounds for stochastic algorithms in the presence of compactness
item.description: arXiv:2602.22741v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a convergence result for sequences of random variables taking values in a metric space that satisfy a stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotonicity condition, in the context of a (local) compactness assumption. Our result is quantitative in that we derive an explicit and effective construction which, in terms of only a few moduli representing quantitative witnesses to key properties of the sequence of random variables and the underlying metric space involved, provides a metastable rate of pointwise convergence, a type of generalized fluctuation bound. That quantitative result in particular relies on the development of a finitary theory of martingales, culminating in a fully finitary Robbins-Siegmund theorem. We outline how this result particularises to the circumstances of the seminal work of Combettes and Pesquet on stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotone sequences in separable Hilbert spaces, and we provide an initial application by illustrating how these results can be used to provide a metastable rate of pointwise convergence for a stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann scheme solving a stochastic common fixed point problem for nonexpansive maps over proper Hadamard spaces. This work is set in the context of recent applications of the logic-based methodology of proof mining to probability theory, and represents its most sophisticated case study to date.
item.dc:creator: Morenikeji Neri, Nicholas Pischke, Thomas Powell

item.title: Counterexamples for lacunary dilates via dyadic spike blocks
item.description: arXiv:2604.18535v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct counterexamples, along dyadic lacunary sequences, to two problems of Erd\H{o}s on the almost-everywhere behavior of sums $\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)$ on the circle. The main device is a dyadic spike block: rare positive spikes, each counted many times by a run of consecutive dilates, make the lacunary averages large, while a deterministic lower bound on every block prevents the rest of the series from cancelling them. We obtain a mean-zero $f\in\bigcap_{1\le q<\infty}L^q(\mathbb T)$ and a sequence $n_j=2^{m_j}$ with $n_{j+1}/n_j\ge2$ such that $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-1/2}$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)=+\infty$ for almost every $x$. This answers negatively a question of Erd\H{o}s on whether the condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log\log N)^{-C}$ suffices for almost-everywhere convergence, and shows that Matsuyama's condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-c}$, $c>1/2$, cannot be relaxed to $c=1/2$. A second choice of parameters gives, for every $2\le p<\infty$, functions $f\in L^p(\mathbb T)$ with $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)/(N(\log N)^{1/p-\varepsilon})=+\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost everywhere. This is sharp up to $\varepsilon$, and the case $p=2$ answers negatively a second question of Erd\H{o}s. Finally, a bounded variant in the spirit of Marstrand's disproof of Khintchine's conjecture gives sets of arbitrarily small measure whose lacunary visiting frequencies have limsup $1$ almost everywhere.
item.dc:creator: Boon Suan Ho

item.title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
item.description: arXiv:2605.08424v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Piening, Richard Duong, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Sharp Error Estimates for a Fully Discrete Approximation of Semilinear Stochastic Convection--Diffusion Equations with Additive Noise and Nonsmooth Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2607.26797v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish sharp strong error estimates for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear stochastic convection--diffusion equations driven by additive noise subject to nonsmooth initial data. The problem is discretized in space using a standard Galerkin finite element method and in time via the linearly implicit Euler scheme. By decoupling the noise regularity index $\beta \in (0, 2]$ from the initial data regularity index $\mu \in (0, 2]$, we derive time-weighted spatial and temporal regularity bounds that isolate the initial singularity at $t = 0$ into an integrable temporal weight. By allowing the drift operator $F$ to map into negative-order fractional spaces to incorporate the convection term, we prove sharp strong convergence rates of order $O(h^\beta + k^{\beta/2})$ for $\beta \in (0, 2)$ and $O\bigl(h^2 + k(1+\ln(t_n/k))^{1/2}\bigr)$ at the critical endpoint $\beta = 2$ for any fixed $t_n > 0$, without requiring the regularity of the initial data to match that of the noise. Furthermore, these convergence rates are achieved under a relaxed differentiability condition requiring only a Lipschitz continuous first G\^ateaux derivative of $F$. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results across both trace-class and space-time white noise regimes.
item.dc:creator: Jitendra Nath Naik, Lok Pati Tripathi

item.title: Discretization and Statistical Consistency of Functional Flow Matching
item.description: arXiv:2608.04531v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Functional flow matching learns to generate random functions, such as velocity fields or solutions of partial differential equations, by continuously transforming a simple probability distribution into a target distribution. In practice, however, training and sampling use only finitely many grid values or coefficients. Does refining these observations recover the intended function-space model, and how do observation, learning, and numerical errors affect the generated distribution? We address these questions by first proving that the velocity targets used for training converge in mean square when the finite reconstructions converge to the underlying functions and remain uniformly bounded. The observations need not be nested: each refinement may replace earlier sensor locations. We also give quantitative bounds for orthogonal projections and extend the result to point observations under suitable regularity and reconstruction assumptions. We then bound the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions in Wasserstein distance, separating observation, learning, numerical, and endpoint errors without requiring uniqueness of the population finite-dimensional dynamics. For a normalized quadrature neural operator representing the learned velocity field, we establish stability and learning bounds with constants independent of the number of sensors. Under fixed model dimension and boundedness assumptions, the statistical excess risk decreases at an inverse-sample-size rate, up to logarithmic factors. A Gaussian example combines these estimates into an explicit sampling-error rate.
item.dc:creator: Lennon J. Shikhman

item.title: The BAR-SOT Method: Long-term Average Cost Control as Stochastic Optimal Self-Transport
item.description: arXiv:2609.17966v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reformulate average-cost (ergodic) control of a Markov jump process as a finite-horizon stochastic optimal transport (SOT) problem that jointly optimizes over the controlled evolution and the marginal law from which it starts and returns to (i.e., a self-transport). The constraint relating the marginal flow to the controlled generator is the basic adjoint relationship (BAR), so we call the resulting problem BAR-SOT. For any time horizon T>0, its optimal value is a constant scaling of the long-run average-cost rate. We give three equivalent formulations (through controlled processes, a Fokker--Planck constraint, and relaxed marginal measures) and show that the optimal dual is a stationary potential plus a term linear in time, with slope equal to the rate. A relative-entropy penalty on the control yields a cost-tilted Schrodinger bridge problem, computable by a Sinkhorn-type iteration when every transition rate is controlled, whose value converges to the unregularized optimum as the penalty vanishes. We develop the theory for finite Markov decision processes and then for general controlled Markov jump processes. A neural parametrization of the dual, trained as a physics-informed neural network (PINN), that encodes Harrison's equivalent-workload formulation (see Harrison 2000) matches the strong reinforcement-learning baseline of Dai and Gluzman (2022); numerically conditioning the fit of a sub-dominant transverse correction then improves on both that baseline and the best priority heuristic. On the input-queued switch, a graph-attention parametrization of the dual improves on the strongest matching heuristic we are aware of, with a parameter count that does not grow with the switch size.
item.dc:creator: Sharan Srinivasan, Berke M. Turkay, Harsha Honnappa

item.title: Christoffel transformations of symmetric $d$-connections and gap probability recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2610.28497v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ of an even discrete weight. For the associated orthogonal polynomial ensembles on squared nodes $y=x^2$, ratios of moment determinants relate the largest-particle distributions and transfer exact gap probability recurrences between the ensembles. For positive weights satisfying the stated moment and support assumptions, this comparison requires no Pearson condition. The transformation is realized by elementary bundle modifications at zero and infinity on $\mathbb P^1$. When the original weight has Pearson ratio $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\mathrm{deg}\; d=1,2$, these modifications conjugate cutoff dynamics on common stable loci of symmetric $d$-connections under the stated geometric hypotheses. The transformed recurrence coefficients are expressed explicitly as rational functions of spectral coordinates. On the unit lattice, a local recurrence formula applies to rational symmetric Pearson ratios of arbitrary degree, including outside these charts, whenever its local hypotheses hold.
item.dc:creator: Anton Selemenchuk

item.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.29238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det \Gamma \ge 1$ for all sublattices $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that (1) $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly log-concave, where $\alpha = 2\pi/e$, and (2) $X + \Lambda$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$. Moreover, the existence of such a density characterizes this property up to a universal dilation. There are a few consequences of the above. We list some. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ \mu(\Lambda, K) = \max_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \left\|x-\lambda\right\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}{\pi}} \cdot \mathbb{E}\,\left\|G\right\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,\mathrm{Id})$. This implies an $O(n \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. We also compare the entire ordered spectrum of the associated flat torus on $\Lambda^*$ with that of a Gaussian, yielding an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem.
item.dc:creator: Brayden Letwin, Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss

item.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.30196v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel. We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.
item.dc:creator: Rundong Ding, Yiyun He, Yizhe Zhu
